body: # Fix session notifications to show title/summary instead of raw query ## Summary This PR fixes a bug where session completion and failure notifications were displaying raw query text instead of the human-readable title or summary. The notifications now follow the same display pattern used throughout the rest of the UI, providing a better user experience. ## Problem Session notifications (both completion and failure) were showing the raw query text in the notification body, which could be: - Technical and hard to understand - Very long and unwieldy - Inconsistent with how sessions are displayed elsewhere in the UI For example, a notification might show: > Completed: find all instances of getCwd in the codebase and rename them to getCurrentWorkingDirectory across all files ensuring consistency Instead of the cleaner summary: > Completed: Rename getCwd to getCurrentWorkingDirectory ## Solution 1. **Created a reusable helper function** `getSessionNotificationText()` that: - Implements the standard fallback pattern: title → summary → query - Truncates text to 40 characters to prevent overly long notifications - Provides TypeScript type safety 2. **Refactored the notification logic** in `Layout.tsx` to use the helper function instead of inline logic 3. **Added comprehensive unit tests** (13 test cases) covering: - Priority logic (title preferred over summary, summary over query) - Text truncation with default and custom lengths - Edge cases (empty strings, undefined values, special characters) - All tests are passing ✅ ## Changes Made - **`humanlayer-wui/src/utils/formatting.ts`**: Added `getSessionNotificationText()` helper function - **`humanlayer-wui/src/utils/formatting.test.ts`**: Created comprehensive unit tests (new file) - **`humanlayer-wui/src/components/Layout.tsx`**: Updated to use the helper function ## User Impact - ✅ Users will see cleaner, more readable notification text - ✅ Notifications are now consistent with the rest of the UI - ✅ Long text is properly truncated to avoid overwhelming notifications - ✅ No breaking changes - this is a pure improvement ## Testing ### Automated Tests - [x] Unit tests pass: `cd humanlayer-wui && bun test src/utils/formatting.test.ts` - [x] TypeScript compilation: `cd humanlayer-wui && npm run typecheck` ### Manual Testing Required - [ ] Launch a Claude Code session and verify completion notification shows the summary - [ ] Cancel a session and verify failure notification shows the summary - [ ] Test with a session that has no title/summary to verify fallback to query works ## Screenshots/Examples ### Before ``` Notification: "Completed: find all instances of getCwd in the codebase and..." ``` ### After ``` Notification: "Completed: Rename getCwd to getCurrentWorking" ``` (Text truncated at 40 characters) ## Migration Notes None - this is a bug fix with no breaking changes. ## Checklist - [x] Code follows the existing patterns in the codebase - [x] Tests have been added/updated - [x] TypeScript types are properly defined - [x] The change is focused and doesn't include unrelated modifications - [ ] Manual testing completed (needs UI verification) ## Related Issues - Fixes ENG-1810: Session completed notifications show summary/last user message instead of session.query ## Additional Notes The 40-character limit for notification text was chosen to balance informativeness with brevity. **Summary**

This PR adds support for the --format parameter to the `wp core verify-checksums` command, enabling structured output formats like `plain, table, json, csv, yaml, count`, and others.

It brings consistency with commands like plugin verify-checksums, improving automation and scripting support.

**✅ Supported formats**
- plain (default)
- table
- json
- csv
- yaml
- count


**🧪 Test Guide**
- Run command in default format: `wp core verify-checksums`
- Run with JSON output: `wp core verify-checksums --format=json`
- Run with CSV output: `wp core verify-checksums --format=csv`

- Trigger an error (e.g., modify a core file) to see results in all formats.

**Notes**
- No breaking changes introduced.
- Falls back to default table if --format is not specified.
- Useful for CI scripts or plugin/tooling integrations.

body:
This PR prepares the `youtube_player_flutter` package for release version 9.1.2, which includes important bug fixes and improvements for better discoverability.

## Changes Made

### Version Bump
- Updated version from `9.1.1` to `9.1.2` in `pubspec.yaml`

### Changelog Updates
Added entry for version 9.1.2 documenting recent bug fixes:
- Fixes type error when handling YouTube error codes (error where int was expected as String)
- Improves error handling for YouTube error codes 150 and 152

### Pub Score Improvements
- Added relevant topics to `pubspec.yaml` for better package discoverability:
  - `youtube`
  - `video` 
  - `player`
  - `iframe`
  - `multimedia`

## Background

The recent commit [75e4669](https://github.com/sarbagyastha/youtube_player_flutter/commit/75e4669de2007c10f9db3dc69f27d0b2b16cef20) fixed critical error handling issues where YouTube error codes could be returned as either `int` or `String` types, causing runtime type errors. The fix added proper type checking in the error handler:

```dart
final errorCode = args.first is int
    ? args.first
    : int.tryParse(args.first) ?? -1;
```

This ensures the player gracefully handles YouTube error codes 150 and 152, which were previously causing crashes due to type mismatches.

## Release Readiness

The package is now ready for release with:
- ✅ Proper version bumping
- ✅ Complete changelog documentation  
- ✅ Enhanced discoverability metadata
- ✅ Stable error handling for all YouTube error scenarios

Fixes #1096.

author: mizzy
body:
## Summary
- Implement hierarchical IAM structure for managing Google Cloud Service APIs with Terraform
- Follow principle of least privilege with minimal custom roles
- Enable secure deployment through service account impersonation

## Architecture

```
iam-for-iam/
├── deploy-iam service account (IAM management)
└── iamManager role (13 permissions)

iam/
├── deploy service account (general deployment)
└── terraformServiceManager role (7 permissions)

main directory/
└── Google Cloud Service API management (Sheets API example)
```

## Key Changes

### IAM Hierarchy
1. **iam-for-iam**: Bootstrap layer for IAM management
2. **iam**: Service account and role management
3. **Main**: Service API enablement/management

### Custom Roles
- `iamManager`: Minimal permissions for IAM resource management
- `terraformServiceManager`: Minimal permissions for Service Usage API

### Security Features
- Service account impersonation instead of direct credentials
- Separate service accounts for different responsibilities
- Support for terraform destroy with necessary undelete permissions

## Limitations
- Conditional IAM policies don't work with Service Usage API disable operations
- True least-privilege cannot be achieved without conditions
- Alternative controls (separate projects, CI/CD approval) recommended for production

## Test Plan
- [x] Create IAM hierarchy with terraform apply
- [x] Enable Google Sheets API
- [x] Test terraform destroy and recreate
- [x] Verify minimal permissions work correctly

Thank you for contributing to DeepInverse!

Please refer to our [contributing guidelines](https://deepinv.github.io/deepinv/contributing.html) for full instructions on how to contribute, including writing tests, documentation and code style.

Once the GitHub tests have been approved by a maintainer (only required for first-time contributors), and the `Build Docs` GitHub action
has run successfully, you can download the documentation as a zip file from the [Actions page](https://github.com/deepinv/deepinv/actions/workflows/documentation.yml). Look for the workflow run corresponding to your pull request.


### Checks to be done before submitting your PR

- [ ] `python3 -m pytest deepinv/tests` runs successfully.
- [ ] `black .` runs successfully.
- [ ] `make html` runs successfully (in the `docs/` directory).
- [ ] Updated docstrings related to the changes (as applicable).
- [ ] Added an entry to the [CHANGELOG.rst](../CHANGELOG.rst).

author: sungeun-yoo
body:
I've refactored the data handling logic to manage all annotations in memory. This prevents data loss when you navigate between images and allows for adding new labels to previously unlabeled images.

Key changes:
- On directory load, all existing JSON files are read into an in-memory state object. Images without JSONs are initialized with an empty annotation structure.
- Image navigation now reads from the in-memory store instead of the file system, preserving any changes made during the session.
- I replaced the 'Save JSON' for a single file with a 'Save All as ZIP' feature. This function iterates through all annotations in memory, creates a JSON file for each, and bundles them into a single downloadable ZIP archive.
- I integrated the JSZip library to handle client-side ZIP creation.
- I also updated the UI elements and event listeners to reflect the new functionality.

body:
This commit refactors the Google login process from a frontend-only implementation to a backend-driven OAuth2 flow.

Changes include:
- Added new backend endpoints `/auth/google/login` and `/auth/google/callback` to handle the OAuth2 flow.
- Added scopes for Google Contacts and Google Calendar API access.
- Created a new `GoogleCalendarService` and ensured the existing `GoogleContactService` is compatible with the new flow.
- Refactored the frontend login page to use the new backend endpoints.
- Added a new frontend route `/auth/callback` to handle the post-login redirect.
- Deprecated the old frontend-driven login flow.

This PR updates [Django](https://pypi.org/project/Django) from **4.0.6** to **5.2.5**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 5.2.5
   ```
   ==========================

*August 6, 2025*

Django 5.2.5 fixes several bugs in 5.2.4.

Bugfixes
========

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2.1 that prevented the usage of ``UNNEST``
  PostgreSQL strategy of ``QuerySet.bulk_create()`` with foreign keys
  (:ticket:`36502`).

* Fixed a crash in Django 5.2 when filtering against a composite primary key
  using a tuple containing expressions (:ticket:`36522`).

* Fixed a crash in Django 5.2 when validating a model that uses
  ``GeneratedField`` or constraints composed of ``Q`` and ``Case`` lookups
  (:ticket:`36518`).

* Added compatibility for ``docutils`` 0.22 (:ticket:`36535`).

* Fixed a crash in Django 5.2 when using a ``ManyToManyField`` on a model with
  a composite primary key, by extending the ``fields.E347`` system check
  (:ticket:`36530`).


==========================
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.2.4
   ```
   ==========================

*July 2, 2025*

Django 5.2.4 fixes several bugs in 5.2.3.

Bugfixes
========

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2.2 where :meth:`HttpRequest.get_preferred_type()
  <django.http.HttpRequest.get_preferred_type>` incorrectly preferred more
  specific media types with a lower quality (:ticket:`36447`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2.3 where ``Value(None, JSONField())`` used in
  a :class:`~django.db.models.expressions.When` condition was incorrectly
  serialized as SQL ``NULL`` instead of JSON ``null`` (:ticket:`36453`).

* Fixed a crash in Django 5.2 when performing an ``__in`` lookup involving a
  composite primary key and a subquery on backends that lack native support for
  tuple lookups (:ticket:`36464`).


==========================
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.2.3
   ```
   ==========================

*June 10, 2025*

Django 5.2.3 fixes several bugs in 5.2.2. Also, the latest string translations
from Transifex are incorporated.

Bugfixes
========

* Fixed a log injection possibility by migrating remaining response logging
  to ``django.utils.log.log_response()``, which safely escapes arguments such
  as the request path to prevent unsafe log output (:cve:`2025-48432`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused :meth:`.QuerySet.bulk_update` to
  incorrectly convert ``None`` to JSON ``null`` instead of SQL ``NULL`` for
  ``JSONField`` (:ticket:`36419`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2.2 where the ``q`` parameter was removed from
  the internal ``django.http.MediaType.params`` property (:ticket:`36446`).


==========================
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.2.2
   ```
   ==========================

*June 4, 2025*

Django 5.2.2 fixes a security issue with severity "low" and several bugs in
5.2.1.

CVE-2025-48432: Potential log injection via unescaped request path
==================================================================

Internal HTTP response logging used ``request.path`` directly, allowing control
characters (e.g. newlines or ANSI escape sequences) to be written unescaped
into logs. This could enable log injection or forgery, letting attackers
manipulate log appearance or structure, especially in logs processed by
external systems or viewed in terminals.

Although this does not directly impact Django's security model, it poses risks
when logs are consumed or interpreted by other tools. To fix this, the internal
``django.utils.log.log_response()`` function now escapes all positional
formatting arguments using a safe encoding.

Bugfixes
========

* Fixed a crash when using ``select_related`` against a ``ForeignObject``
  originating from a model with a ``CompositePrimaryKey`` (:ticket:`36373`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 5.2 where subqueries using ``"pk"`` to reference models
  with a ``CompositePrimaryKey`` failed to raise ``ValueError`` when too many
  or too few columns were selected (:ticket:`36392`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused a crash when no arguments were
  passed into ``QuerySet.union()`` (:ticket:`36388`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 where subclasses of ``RemoteUserMiddleware``
  that had overridden ``process_request()`` were no longer supported
  (:ticket:`36390`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused a crash when using ``OuterRef``
  in the ``filter`` argument of an ``Aggregate`` expression (:ticket:`36404`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused a crash when using ``OuterRef``
  in PostgreSQL aggregate functions ``ArrayAgg``, ``StringAgg``, and
  ``JSONBAgg`` (:ticket:`36405`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 where admin's ``filter_horizontal`` buttons
  lacked ``type="button"``, causing them to intercept form submission when
  pressing the Enter key (:ticket:`36423`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 5.2 where calling ``QuerySet.in_bulk()`` with an
  ``id_list`` argument on models with a ``CompositePrimaryKey`` failed to
  observe database parameter limits (:ticket:`36416`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 5.2 where :meth:`HttpRequest.get_preferred_type()
  <django.http.HttpRequest.get_preferred_type>` did not account for media type
  parameters in ``Accept`` headers, reducing specificity in content negotiation
  (:ticket:`36411`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused a crash when using
  ``QuerySet.prefetch_related()`` to prefetch a foreign key with a ``Prefetch``
  queryset for a subclass of the foreign target (:ticket:`36432`).


==========================
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.2.1
   ```
   ==========================

*May 7, 2025*

Django 5.2.1 fixes a security issue with severity "moderate" and several bugs
in 5.2.

This release was built using an upgraded :pypi:`setuptools`, producing
filenames compliant with :pep:`491` and :pep:`625` and thus addressing a PyPI
warning about non-compliant distribution filenames. This change only affects
the Django packaging process and does not impact Django's behavior.

CVE-2025-32873: Denial-of-service possibility in ``strip_tags()``
=================================================================

:func:`~django.utils.html.strip_tags` would be slow to evaluate certain inputs
containing large sequences of incomplete HTML tags. This function is used to
implement the :tfilter:`striptags` template filter, which was thus also
vulnerable.

:func:`~django.utils.html.strip_tags` now raises a :exc:`.SuspiciousOperation`
exception if it encounters an unusually large number of unclosed opening tags.

Bugfixes

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused unnecessary queries when

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused a crash of

author: olii-dev
body:
This pull request introduces dynamic weather functionality to the homepage, replacing the previous static weather information for Adelaide. The main change is the integration of live weather data using the wttr.in API, which updates automatically and provides fallback content if the service is unavailable. Additionally, the page load logic is updated to accommodate both layout and weather initialization.

**Weather widget enhancements:**

* The static weather description in `index.html` is replaced with a dynamic container (`weather-content`) that is populated by JavaScript with live weather data.
* A new asynchronous `fetchWeather` function in `script.js` fetches current weather data for Adelaide from the wttr.in API, parses the response, and updates the weather widget. It includes a fallback to static content if the API is unavailable.
* A helper function `getWeatherEmoji` maps weather codes to appropriate emojis for a richer user experience.
* Weather data is refreshed automatically every 30 minutes to ensure up-to-date information.

**Page load and event management:**

* The page load event handler is updated to call both `loadLayout` and `fetchWeather` on page load, ensuring the layout and weather information are initialized together. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ed3ee7e0beea2498ff3b8ca85973d122fc6fa3d585d62b5807ec034d0cf076b3L46-L47) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ed3ee7e0beea2498ff3b8ca85973d122fc6fa3d585d62b5807ec034d0cf076b3R67-R140)

This PR adds comprehensive GitHub Copilot developer instructions to enable efficient coding work in the film-finder repository. The instructions were created through exhaustive validation of all build, test, and run commands with precise timing measurements.

## What's Added

- **Validated command sequences** with exact timing data (Python deps: 27s, React deps: 6.5min, React build: 21s)
- **Critical timeout warnings** for long-running operations with explicit "NEVER CANCEL" guidance
- **End-to-end manual validation scenarios** for both Python/Dash and React interfaces
- **Expected network failures** documentation (JustWatch API, OMDB API blocked in sandboxed environments)
- **File structure reference** and common modification points
- **Troubleshooting guide** for build failures and runtime issues

## Application Architecture Documented

The instructions cover the dual-interface architecture:

1. **Python/Dash Backend** (`app.py`) - Dark-themed data table with streaming integration
2. **React/TypeScript Frontend** (`frontend/`) - Modern card-based UI with advanced filtering

Both share the same film database (`data/clean.csv`) containing 7,628+ films with IMDB ratings, genres, and metadata.

## Manual Validation Completed

All instructions were thoroughly tested through complete user workflows:

- ✅ Python/Dash application runs successfully on port 8050
- ✅ React frontend runs successfully on port 3000  
- ✅ Search functionality works ("batman" returns 12 films)
- ✅ Filtering, pagination, and sorting operate correctly
- ✅ Network-dependent features fail predictably (expected in sandbox)

## Key Features for Developers

- **Exact timeout values** to prevent premature build cancellation
- **Step-by-step validation scenarios** for manual testing
- **Clear expectation setting** for API failures in restricted environments
- **Quick reference** for common development tasks and file locations

The instructions follow best practices with imperative tone and exhaustive validation to ensure any GitHub Copilot agent can work effectively with this codebase from day one.

# Description

I have successfully reimplemented the video functionalities as requested. Here's a summary of what has been accomplished:

*   **New `Video` Class:** The core video processing logic is now consolidated within the `supervision.Video` class, providing a modern and intuitive API.
*   **Multi-Backend Support:** The implementation includes both OpenCV and PyAV backends, which can be selected during `Video` object instantiation. This addresses the need for more reliable video metadata retrieval, as highlighted in the linked GitHub issue.
*   **Feature Parity:** All functionalities from the old video API, such as frame iteration, video saving with callbacks, and manual control over video sinking, are available in the new implementation.
*   **Deprecation:** The old video functions and classes in `supervision.utils.video` have been marked as deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Their internals have been refactored to use the new `Video` class, ensuring a smooth transition.
*   **Unit Tests:** A comprehensive suite of unit tests has been added for the new `Video` class, covering both backends and ensuring the reliability of the implementation.
*   **Documentation:** The official documentation has been updated to reflect the new API, with the old documentation removed and new pages and docstrings added for the `Video` class and its components.

All the necessary files have been created, modified, and tested to meet the requirements of the task.

body:
This PR provides a comprehensive analysis of the FitMatch app's current state to determine which tests would likely pass or fail, and estimates the overall app completeness percentage.

## Analysis Results

**Key Findings:**
- **68% of theoretical tests would PASS** based on current implementation
- **App completeness is at 68%** (if 100% passing tests = 100% complete app)

## Test Pass/Fail Breakdown by Feature Category

The analysis evaluated 9 major feature categories:

- **Authentication & User Management: 85% PASS** - Strong foundation with complete login/signup flow
- **User Profiles & Onboarding: 80% PASS** - Well-implemented with sports, diet, and personality choices
- **Legal & Compliance: 90% PASS** - Nearly complete with all required legal pages
- **Core App Features: 70% PASS** - Good basics including swipe functionality and profile cards
- **Events Management: 65% PASS** - Basic CRUD operations implemented
- **Advertising System: 60% PASS** - Basic ad management without advanced targeting
- **Social Features: 60% PASS** - Missing real-time messaging and notifications
- **Business/Partner Features: 55% PASS** - Basic implementation, lacks verification
- **Technical Infrastructure: 45% PASS** - Critical issues with missing Redux store files

## Critical Issues Identified

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements advanced header UI customization functionality for super administrators, allowing complete control over navigation button positioning, styling, and layout as requested in the original issue.

## Problem Addressed

The original request was for header UI configuration options that would allow super admins to:
- Modify button location per button (vertically center and so on)
- Modify button location horizontally  
- Modify button colors and styling
- Provide CSS override capabilities

## Solution Implemented

### New Header Customization Features

![Header Customization Demo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a13272c8-e877-4c3a-93b7-08e7a88b5232)

**1. Global Button Alignment**
- Options: Default, Left, Center, Right, Justify (space-between)
- Controls horizontal positioning of all navigation buttons using CSS flexbox

**2. Vertical Button Alignment**  
- Options: Top, Center, Bottom
- Controls vertical positioning within header height
- Allows buttons to be aligned to header top, center, or bottom

**3. Custom Button Spacing**
- Configurable gap between navigation buttons
- Supports CSS units (px, rem, em, %)
- Default: 15px

**4. Individual Button Customization**
Each header button (Dashboard, Manage Screens, Admin Panel, User Dropdown) can be customized individually:

- **Position Controls**: Margin Top/Right/Bottom/Left, Display Order for reordering
- **Color Controls**: Text Color, Background Color, Hover states for both
- **Real-time color picker** with hex input validation

**5. Header-Specific CSS Override**
- Dedicated CSS injection field for advanced header customization
- Applied after all other header styles for maximum control
- Separate from global CSS customization

**6. Real-Time Preview**
- Live preview section showing header with current settings
- Instant feedback for all customization changes

## Technical Implementation

### Backend Changes
- **Database Migration**: Added version 6 migration with 6 new UI settings
- **API Extension**: Updated `/api/admin/ui-settings` endpoints
- **New Settings**:
  - `header_button_alignment` - Global horizontal alignment
  - `header_button_vertical_alignment` - Global vertical alignment  
  - `header_button_spacing` - Configurable button spacing
  - `header_button_individual_positions` - JSON object for per-button positioning
  - `header_button_individual_colors` - JSON object for per-button colors
  - `header_custom_css` - Header-specific CSS injection

### Frontend Changes
- **ThemeContext Enhancement**: Added comprehensive header button styling logic
- **New UI Section**: "Header Button Customization (Super Admin)" in CloudUICustomization
- **Individual Controls**: Detailed per-button positioning and color customization
- **State Management**: Proper JSON parsing/serialization for complex settings
- **Responsive Design**: Grid layout adapting to different screen sizes

### CSS Generation
The system dynamically generates CSS based on settings:

```css
/* Global header button styling */
.header .nav-links {
  justify-content: center; /* Based on alignment setting */
  align-items: flex-start; /* Based on vertical alignment */
  gap: 20px; /* Based on spacing setting */
}

/* Individual button styling */
.header .nav-link[href="/"] {
  color: #ff0000; /* Individual color */
  background-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.1); /* Individual background */
  margin-top: 5px; /* Individual positioning */
  order: 2; /* Custom display order */
}
```

## Security & Access Control
- **Super Admin Only**: Feature restricted to users with `is_admin` flag
- **Input Validation**: All settings validated on backend
- **CSS Sanitization**: Custom CSS properly handled for security
- **Database Security**: Settings stored securely with proper escaping

## User Experience
- **Intuitive Interface**: Clear labels and descriptions for all options
- **Visual Feedback**: Real-time preview of changes
- **Easy Reset**: Individual button reset functionality  
- **Responsive Design**: Works on all screen sizes
- **Consistent Design**: Matches existing UI customization patterns

## Usage
1. Access: Admin Panel → UI Customization (Super Admin required)
2. Scroll to "Header Button Customization (Super Admin)" section
3. Configure global settings (alignment, spacing)
4. Customize individual buttons (position, colors)
5. Add custom CSS for advanced styling
6. Preview changes in real-time
7. Save settings to apply system-wide

This implementation provides the requested functionality while maintaining system security, performance, and architectural consistency with the existing UI customization system.

body: Refactor `AccessibilityService` to move text insertion logic to companion object static methods, resolving "Unresolved reference" errors. The previous implementation attempted to call instance methods (`insertTextInternal`) from within the `companion object`'s `insertText` method. Kotlin's access rules prevent companion objects from directly accessing instance methods, even if they are `internal`, leading to compilation failures. This refactoring resolves the access permission issue by making all relevant text insertion logic static within the companion object. ---

author: simon-20
body:
This PR is for an initial working version of the IATI Data Downloader, which works as per [the specification here](https://github.com/IATI/iati-message-queue-service/). It receives download request messages from Azure Service Bus, attempts to download and if successful uploads to the IATI dataset cache, and then sends a results message back for consumption by the Bulk Data Service app.

Much of this code comes from the Bulk Data Service, as this is part of the Bulk Data Service refactor, to use message passing to allow horizontal scaling of downloads.

Unit and integration tests are included and cover the core functionality (integration tests employ a docker compose setup with the Azurite emulator and Mockoon service).

Automated deployment to Azure Functions has not yet been done - I thought it was best to get this PR underway so the review could happen in parallel with the CD setup, which can be put in another PR.

(I've created issue #2 for adding a GitHub Action deployment, #3 for setting up robust logging, and #4 for adding Sentry to this app - those are the main things left to do for this.)

## Purpose

Fix issues with the missed sessions UI where the "mark as done" button wasn't working and redistributed sessions were still appearing in the missed sessions list. The goal is to improve the logic for handling missed sessions by ensuring proper filtering and providing functional completion buttons.

## Code changes

### StudyPlanView.tsx
- **Enhanced missed session filtering**: Added logic to exclude redistributed and completed sessions from the missed sessions list
- **Fixed mark done functionality**: Implemented `handleMarkMissedSessionDone` function to properly mark individual sessions as completed
- **Improved UI clarity**: 
  - Added "Mark Done" buttons for individual sessions
  - Renamed "Mark as Done" to "Mark Task Done" for overdue tasks to distinguish between session and task completion
  - Updated help text to clarify different action types
  - Changed button styling for task completion (blue) vs session completion (purple)

### scheduling.ts
- **Enhanced redistribution tracking**: Set session status to 'redistributed' instead of 'scheduled' when moving missed sessions
- **Added redistribution metadata**: Include detailed reschedule history with timestamps, reasons, and success status
- **Improved session tracking**: Added `rescheduledAt` timestamp and comprehensive metadata to prevent redistributed sessions from appearing as missed

These changes ensure that:
1. The "Mark Done" button now works correctly for individual sessions
2. Successfully redistributed sessions no longer appear in the missed sessions UI
3. Better distinction between marking individual sessions vs entire tasks as complete

author: dskarzh
body:
Duration alarm rules are evaluated periodically in the background. When a duration alarm rule contains a dynamic duration value, it retrieves data from the associated entity (e.g., current tenant or device). For device-specific dynamic values, the node looks up the value in the data snapshot stored in AlarmState. This data snapshot is initialized lazily when messages (such as telemetry data) are received from the device.

NPE occurs when duration alarm rules with dynamic values attempt to access an uninitialized data snapshot. This happens in scenario where no messages have been received from a device, leaving the data snapshot null.

author: copilot
body:
This PR addresses critical issues in the Termchat client that were causing message duplication, UI corruption, and poor user experience. The changes restore reliable communication with the termchat backend while significantly improving the interface design.

## Issues Fixed

**Communication Protocol Problems:**
- Message duplication and corruption due to multiple WebSocket listeners
- Connection state management issues causing ghost messages
- Missing timeout handling for WebSocket operations
- Inadequate error recovery when connections drop

**UI Rendering Issues:**
- Severe layout corruption with repeated form elements appearing outside containers
- Complex CSS layouts causing rendering glitches in Textual framework
- Poor spacing and cramped interface elements
- Missing auto-focus functionality

## Key Changes

**Enhanced WebSocket Communication:**
```python
# Added proper connection state management
self._listening: bool = False  # Prevent duplicate listeners

# Improved message handling with timeouts
message = await asyncio.wait_for(self.websocket.recv(), timeout=60.0)

# Better error recovery and connection cleanup
if not self.websocket.closed and self.connected:
    # Only send if truly connected
```

**Simplified, Robust UI Design:**
- Replaced complex container layouts with straightforward vertical arrangement
- Implemented pure OLED black background (#000000) throughout the application
- Added proper auto-focus to input fields for better UX
- Cleaned up CSS to eliminate rendering conflicts

**Connection Dialog Improvements:**
```python
# Clean, minimal layout that actually renders correctly
yield Label("=== TERMCHAT CONNECTION ===")
yield Label("Username:")
yield Input(placeholder="Enter username", id="username_input")
# ... clean vertical flow without containers
```

## Benefits

- **Reliable Messaging**: No more duplicate or corrupted messages
- **Clean Interface**: Professional OLED black theme with proper spacing
- **Better UX**: Auto-focus and intuitive navigation
- **Stable Rendering**: Eliminated UI corruption issues entirely
- **Maintainable Code**: Simplified architecture that's easier to debug

## Testing

The application now displays a clean connection dialog without rendering artifacts and successfully handles WebSocket communication without message duplication. The OLED black theme provides excellent readability while the simplified layout ensures consistent behavior across different terminal environments.

Fixes the core communication protocol issues while delivering the requested UI improvements in a minimal, surgical approach.

body: [Jira](https://gov-uk.atlassian.net/jira/software/c/projects/WHIT/boards/401?selectedIssue=WHIT-1517) ### Why This refactoring improves the user experience of Whitehall's publishing workflow—specifically in how embedded contact IDs in Govspeak content are validated within both Editions and HTML attachments. Previously, Whitehall allowed users to create and publish content containing HTML attachments that may have become invalid over time. This could happen due to: - Validation rules being introduced or tightened after initial publication - Contacts being deleted or changed, rendering existing embeds invalid As a result, users might only discover issues at publish time(usually when making a new edition)—despite having made no changes to the attachment. ### What This PR introduces a context-aware validation system for embedded contacts in Govspeak content that: - Surfaces clear, specific errors in the UI when validation fails - Skips certain validations during draft creation to unblock editors from fixing invalid editions **BEFORE** **AFTER** **BEFORE** **AFTER**

author: jcbrill
body:
Provide explicit error messages for tempfile encoding failures and reduce the likelihood of an open tempfile file handle at exit.

Based on discussions #4749, #4746, and #4752.

Changes to `TempFileMunge` (`SCons\.Platform\.__init__.py`):
* Move encoding the tempfile contents before creating the tempfile due to possible encoding errors.
* Ensure the tempfile file handle is closed after writing the tempfile contents.
* Raise a `TempFileEncodeError` exception when the tempfile contents encoding fails for known exception types.

Example `TempFileEncodeError` exceptions:

* `UnicodeEncodeError` (user-defined encoding):
  ```
  scons: *** [src\main.obj] TempFileEncodeError : [UnicodeEncodeError] 'charmap' codec can't encode characters in position 85-86: character maps to <undefined>
    TempFileMunge encoding: env['TEMPFILEENCODING'] = 'cp1252'
  Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  SCons.Platform.TempFileEncodeError: [UnicodeEncodeError] 'charmap' codec can't encode characters in position 85-86: character maps to <undefined>
    TempFileMunge encoding: env['TEMPFILEENCODING'] = 'cp1252'
  ```

* `LookupError` (user-defined encoding):
  ```
  scons: *** [src\main.obj] TempFileEncodeError : [LookupError] unknown encoding: notinstalled
    TempFileMunge encoding: env['TEMPFILEENCODING'] = 'notinstalled'
  Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  SCons.Platform.TempFileEncodeError: [LookupError] unknown encoding: notinstalled
    TempFileMunge encoding: env['TEMPFILEENCODING'] = 'notinstalled'
  ```

* `TypeError` (user-defined encoding):
  ```
  scons: *** [src\main.obj] TempFileEncodeError : [TypeError] bytes() argument 'encoding' must be str, not None
    TempFileMunge encoding: env['TEMPFILEENCODING'] = None
  Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  SCons.Platform.TempFileEncodeError: [TypeError] bytes() argument 'encoding' must be str, not None
    TempFileMunge encoding: env['TEMPFILEENCODING'] = None
  ```

* `UnicodeError` (user-modified default encoding):
  ```
  scons: *** [src\main.obj] TempFileEncodeError : [UnicodeEncodeError] 'charmap' codec can't encode characters in position 85-86: character maps to <undefined>
    TempFileMunge encoding: default = 'cp1252'
  Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  SCons.Platform.TempFileEncodeError: [UnicodeEncodeError] 'charmap' codec can't encode characters in position 85-86: character maps to <undefined>
    TempFileMunge encoding: default = 'cp1252'
  ```
  
The `TempFileEncodeError` exception text contains:
* The exception name (`TempFileEncodeError`) is an indication what failed.
* The underlying exception name (`[UnicodeEncodeError]`) and reason is an indication of why it failed.
* The `TempFileMunge` line indicates if a user-defined encoding value was defined or the default encoding value was used and/or modified.

If nothing else, this should make it easier to decipher what us happening should the exception text be posted in the mailing list or in an issue.

Not addressed:
* The tempfile removal invocation (i.e., `os.remove(file)`) in the `atexit` handler has not been changed.  Moving the tempfile encoding before the tempfile is opened and closing the tempfile on write errors should reduce the likelihood of errors upon removal.  However, anti-virus software could always be a problem.

Feature complete: no additional changes planned.

## Contributor Checklist:

* [x] I have created a new test or updated the unit tests to cover the new/changed functionality.
* [x] I have updated `CHANGES.txt` and `RELEASE.txt` (and read the `README.rst`).
* [ ] I have updated the appropriate documentation

## Summary
Implements a unified, reusable AI model selector component that provides consistent model selection across the application with role-based access control (RBAC) and capability-based filtering.

Closes #99

## What Changed

### ✨ New Features
- **Unified Model Selector Component**: Single reusable component for all model selection needs
- **Role-Based Access Control**: Models are filtered based on user's assigned roles
- **Capability Filtering**: Only shows models with required capabilities (e.g., "chat")
- **User Roles API**: New endpoint to fetch current user's roles for client-side filtering

### 🔧 Improvements
- **Consistent UI/UX**: Same model selection experience across chat, compare, and assistant architect
- **Better Accessibility**: Proper ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, screen reader support
- **Performance**: Virtualization for large model lists, optimized re-renders
- **Cleaner Display**: Removed model IDs from dropdowns, added descriptions consistently

### 🐛 Bug Fixes
- Fixed mouse scrolling in sheet-based model selectors
- Fixed JSONB type casting for capabilities and allowed_roles
- Fixed role settings not persisting after page reload
- Removed deprecated chat_enabled field dependencies

```
components/features/model-selector/
├── index.ts                       # Public exports
├── model-selector.tsx             # Main component
├── model-selector-item.tsx        # Individual model display
├── use-filtered-models.ts         # Filtering logic hook
├── model-selector-form-adapter.tsx # react-hook-form adapter
└── model-selector-types.ts        # TypeScript definitions
```

### Integration Points
1. **Chat Page** (`/chat`) - For single model selection
2. **Compare Page** (`/compare`) - For comparing two models
3. **Assistant Architect** (`/utilities/assistant-architect`) - For prompt configuration

### Database Changes
- Added `allowed_roles` JSONB column to `ai_models` table
- Migration ensures backward compatibility
- Updated existing models with ["chat"] capability

## Testing

- ✅ Verified capability filtering (only chat-capable models shown)
- ✅ Confirmed role-based access control
- ✅ Tested mouse and keyboard scrolling

Model selector shows:

None - all changes are backward compatible

- [x] Performance optimizations applied

author: laurabeatris
body:
## Description

This PR introduces a new API to navigate on `setActive`, that can be leveraged for after-auth flows to handle pending sessions, featuring a callback mechanism that enables developers to integrate their application logic, such as navigation. 

Previously, our flows were mistakenly navigating after `setActive`, which could cause issues with session revalidation and re-render of pages.

From now on, we're proposing two options to deal with after-auth: `taskUrls` or `navigate`

### `navigate`

A callback function that can be provided as an `setActive` option.

```ts
setActive({ 
  navigate: async ({ session }) => { 
     const currentTask = session.currentTask; 

     if (currentTask){ 
      // Developer has full control over navigation logic
      // (this also allows our AIO components to pass their navigation context such as modal routing)
       await router.push(`/onboarding/${currentTask.key}`)
       return 
     }

    await router.push('/dashboard')
  }
})
```

### `taskUrls` (existing)

A map of URLs per session task key that can be provided as a Clerk option. On `setActive`, it'll be used for navigation.

```tsx
<ClerkProvider 
   taskUrls={{'choose-organization': '/onboarding/choose-organization' }}
/>
```

# 🚀 **Migrate to pnpm Package Manager**

## 📝 **Overview**

This PR migrates the project from npm to pnpm as the primary package manager. pnpm offers significant improvements in performance, disk space efficiency, and dependency management while maintaining full compatibility with npm.

## 🎯 **Why pnpm?**

- **⚡ Faster installs**: pnpm is typically 2x faster than npm due to its linking strategy
- **💾 Disk space efficiency**: Uses hard links and symlinks to avoid duplicate packages
- **🔒 Strict dependency resolution**: Prevents phantom dependencies and ensures reproducible builds
- **🏗️ Monorepo support**: Better workspace management (future-proofing)
- **📦 npm compatibility**: Works with existing npm packages and registries

## 🔧 **Changes Made**

### **package.json**

- Added `"packageManager": "pnpm@10.10.0"` to specify the recommended pnpm version
- Updated CSS build scripts to use `pnpm exec` instead of `npx`:
  - `ui_css`: `pnpm exec esbuild --bundle public/css/_ui.css --outfile=public/css/ui.css`
  - `mapp_css`: `pnpm exec esbuild --bundle public/css/_mapp.css --outfile=public/css/mapp.css`

### **.gitignore**

- Added `pnpm-lock.yaml` to ignore list (lock file should not be committed for libraries)
- Added `.pnpm-store/` to ignore pnpm's local store directory
- Kept `package-lock.json` and `yarn.lock` in ignore list for legacy cleanup

## 🚀 **How to Use pnpm**

### **Installation**

If you don't have pnpm installed globally:

```bash
npm install -g pnpm@10.10.0
# or
curl -fsSL https://get.pnpm.io/install.sh | sh -
```

### **Basic Commands**

| npm command            | pnpm equivalent                        | Description              |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `npm install`          | `pnpm install`                         | Install all dependencies |
| `npm install <pkg>`    | `pnpm add <pkg>`                       | Add a dependency         |
| `npm install -D <pkg>` | `pnpm add -D <pkg>`                    | Add a dev dependency     |
| `npm uninstall <pkg>`  | `pnpm remove <pkg>`                    | Remove a dependency      |
| `npm run <script>`     | `pnpm run <script>` or `pnpm <script>` | Run a script             |
| `npx <command>`        | `pnpm exec <command>`                  | Execute a package binary |

### **xyz Commands**

```bash
# Install dependencies
pnpm install

# Install dev dependencies
pnpm install --dev

# Install prod dependencies (pnpm will not install any package listed in devDependencies)
pnpm install --prod

# Install no optional dependencies
pnpm install --no-optional

# Run tests
pnpm test
pnpm test-watch

# Build CSS
pnpm ui_css
pnpm mapp_css

# Generate documentation
pnpm generate-docs
pnpm mapp-docs
pnpm xyz-docs
pnpm test-docs

# Build project
pnpm _build
```

## ✅ **Verification**

The migration has been tested and verified:

- ✅ All 168 existing tests pass with pnpm
- ✅ CSS build scripts work correctly
- ✅ All dependencies install successfully (357 packages)
- ✅ Documentation generation works as expected

## 🔄 **Migration for Team Members**

1. **Install pnpm** (if not already installed):

   ```bash
   npm install -g pnpm@10.10.0
   ```

2. **Clean up old npm artifacts**:

   ```bash
   rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json
   ```
   Note if clearing up from a VSCode Terminal you can use this command 
   ``` bash  
    Remove-Item -Recurse -Force node_modules, package-lock.json
    ```

3. **Install dependencies with pnpm**:

   ```bash
   pnpm install
   ```

## 📊 **Performance Benefits**

After migration, you should notice:

- **Faster dependency installation** (typically 50-75% faster)
- **Reduced disk usage** in `node_modules`
- **More reliable builds** due to stricter dependency resolution
- **Better caching** across projects

## 🤝 **Compatibility**

- ✅ All existing npm packages work with pnpm
- ✅ All npm scripts continue to work
- ✅ CI/CD pipelines need minimal changes (just replace `npm` with `pnpm`)
- ✅ IDE integrations work seamlessly

## 📚 **Additional Resources**

- [pnpm Documentation](https://pnpm.io/)
- [pnpm vs npm vs yarn](https://pnpm.io/benchmarks)
- [Migration Guide](https://pnpm.io/installation)

---

**Note**: This change is backward compatible - team members can continue using npm temporarily, but pnpm is now the recommended and optimized package manager for xyz.

## Summary
Implements a comprehensive AWS discovery system that finds ALL resources regardless of whether they are tagged or not, addressing critical gaps in VPC, subnet, and security group discovery.

## Type of Change
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] ⚡ Performance improvements
- [x] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] 🎨 Code style/formatting changes
- [x] 🔧 Build/CI changes

## Related Issues
Addresses user feedback about missing untagged infrastructure resources including VPCs, subnets, and security groups.

## Changes Made
### Core Discovery System
- **New `ComprehensiveAWSDiscovery` class** with service-specific API discovery
- **Enhanced discovery strategy**: Service APIs → Tag enrichment → Billing validation
- **22+ AWS services support** including EC2, S3, RDS, Lambda, IAM, CloudFront, Route53
- **Parallel processing** with ThreadPoolExecutor for improved performance
- **Smart caching and circuit breakers** for resilient operation

### Infrastructure Discovery Improvements
- **VPCs, subnets, security groups** now discovered regardless of tags
- **Network infrastructure** (IGWs, NAT gateways, route tables, NACLs)
- **Global service handling** (S3, IAM, CloudFront, Route53)
- **Regional service optimization** with proper region handling

### Performance Enhancements
- **5-8 resources/second performance** (68% above targets)
- **93-97% parallel efficiency** in real-world testing
- **Graceful error handling** with permission failures
- **Resource deduplication and normalization**

### Code Quality & Maintenance
- **Fixed duplicate logging issues** with proper logger hierarchy
- **Code formatting with Black** for consistent style
- **Import cleanup** and linting improvements
- **Enhanced error handling** and debugging support

### Documentation & Templates
- **Comprehensive discovery documentation** in Docusaurus
- **GitHub issue templates** for bugs, features, and questions
- **Pull request template** with detailed checklists
- **Updated README** highlighting new capabilities
- **Set Docusaurus to light theme** by default

## Testing
### Test Environment
- [x] Local testing completed
- [x] AWS account testing completed (Account: 247549961578)
- [x] Documentation examples verified
- [x] Performance benchmarking completed

### Test Commands
```bash
# Comprehensive discovery test
./inventag.sh --create-excel --create-word --enable-production-safety

# Direct API testing
python3 -c "
from inventag.discovery.comprehensive_discovery import ComprehensiveAWSDiscovery
discovery = ComprehensiveAWSDiscovery(regions=['us-east-1'])
resources = discovery.discover_all_resources()
print(f'Found {len(resources)} resources')
"
```

### Test Results
- ✅ **117 total resources discovered** vs 104 with ResourceGroupsTagging only
- ✅ **17 VPC/network resources found** vs 0 previously  
- ✅ **Performance: 5.2-8.4 resources/sec** (exceeds 5.0 target by 68%)
- ✅ **Both tagged and untagged resources** discovered successfully
- ✅ **No regression in existing functionality**

## AWS Services Affected
- [x] EC2 (VPCs, subnets, security groups, instances, volumes)
- [x] S3 (buckets with region detection)
- [x] RDS (instances, clusters, snapshots)
- [x] Lambda (functions, layers)
- [x] IAM (users, roles, policies - global)
- [x] CloudFront (distributions - global)
- [x] Route53 (hosted zones - global)
- [x] ELB/ALB (load balancers, target groups)
- [x] KMS (keys, aliases)
- [x] CloudWatch (alarms, dashboards)
- [x] ECS/EKS (clusters, services)
- [x] SNS/SQS (topics, queues)
- [x] DynamoDB (tables)
- [x] API Gateway (REST APIs)

## Breaking Changes
**Migration required for users relying on ResourceGroupsTagging-only discovery:**

The system now uses service-specific APIs as the primary discovery method. This provides complete resource coverage but changes the discovery approach:

- **Before**: ResourceGroupsTagging API only → missed untagged resources
- **After**: Service-specific APIs primary → ResourceGroupsTagging enrichment → complete coverage

**Backward compatibility maintained** via `use_comprehensive=False` parameter.

## Documentation
- [x] Code comments added/updated
- [x] README updated with comprehensive discovery features
- [x] Documentation site updated with new architecture guide
- [x] Examples added for comprehensive discovery usage
- [x] GitHub templates created for better issue management

- **Discovery speed**: 5.2-8.4 resources/second (68% above 5.0 target)
- **Resource coverage**: +13 additional resources (13% improvement)  
- **VPC/Network discovery**: 0 → 17 resources (infinite improvement)
- **Parallel efficiency**: 93-97% worker utilization
- **Execution time**: 33-35 seconds for comprehensive discovery

## Additional Notes
This implementation directly addresses the critical user feedback: *"it must prioritize using service-specific APIs to get all services, regardless tagged or not... things like vpc must be able to reflect"*

### Key Achievements:
1. **Complete infrastructure visibility** - no more missing VPCs or untagged resources
2. **Maintained compatibility** - existing workflows continue to work
3. **Enhanced performance** - significantly faster than previous approaches
4. **Production-tested** - verified on real AWS account with comprehensive coverage
5. **Comprehensive documentation** - full guides and examples provided

The system successfully finds resources like `vpc-3fcb1945` (untagged) alongside `vpc-00a01f0f961f9f769` (tagged), providing the complete AWS resource landscape that was previously missing.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The original implementation had several limitations that prevented seamless project creation, deployment, and local development:

1. **Forced subdirectory creation** - Users couldn't create projects in their current directory
2. **Basic Coolify integration** - Limited credential verification and storage
3. **Case-sensitive Docker tags** - Caused deployment failures in Coolify
4. **No PR deployment automation** - Manual deployment management for feature branches
5. **Manual service setup** - Required users to manually configure databases, cache, and AI services in Coolify
6. **Complex local development** - No easy way to get local development environment running quickly
7. **Manual webhook management** - Deployment webhooks not automatically retrieved and stored

## Solution

Enhanced the CLI with comprehensive improvements for complete infrastructure automation and instant local development:

### Instant Local Development Environment
```bash
# One-click local development setup
./setup-dev.sh

# Or use npm scripts
npm run services:start    # Start all local services instantly
npm run dev              # Start SvelteKit development
npm run services:stop    # Clean shutdown
```

### Automatic Webhook Management
- **Webhook auto-retrieval** - automatically fetches deployment webhook URLs from Coolify API
- **Environment storage** - saves webhook URLs to `.env` as `COOLIFY_WEBHOOK_URL` for easy access
- **Deployment automation** - `npm run deploy:trigger` uses stored webhook for instant deployments
- **GitHub Actions integration** - workflows automatically use environment webhook variables

### Comprehensive Coolify Auto-Provisioning
- **Complete infrastructure automation** - automatically creates and configures all needed services
- **SvelteKit Docker deployment** with health checks, auto-deployment webhooks, and optimized container configuration
- **Database services** (PocketBase or MongoDB) with persistent storage and authentication
- **Redis cache** with password protection and persistent volumes
- **LiteLLM AI Gateway** supporting OpenAI, Anthropic, and other LLM providers
- **Qdrant vector database** for AI embeddings and semantic search
- **Project networking** - dedicated network connecting all services for inter-service communication
- **Service discovery** - internal DNS resolution for seamless service connectivity

### Enhanced Developer Experience
- **One-click setup script** - `./setup-dev.sh` checks Docker, starts services, and provides guidance
- **Local service orchestration** - `docker-compose.dev.yml` with all services for local development
- **Comprehensive npm scripts** - `services:start/stop/logs`, `dev:setup`, `deploy:trigger`
- **Health monitoring** - `/health` endpoint that monitors all service connectivity and status
- **Dual environment configuration** - separate URLs for local development and production services
- **Service documentation** - detailed README with service URLs, configuration, and usage examples

### Current Directory Support
```bash
# Now supports both approaches:
npx skit-fast cli my-project     # Creates subdirectory
npx skit-fast cli               # Creates in current directory (empty name)
npx skit-fast cli .             # Creates in current directory (explicit)
```

## Key Features

### Local Development Automation
- **Docker environment validation** - setup script checks for Docker and Docker Compose
- **Service startup coordination** - proper dependency management and health checks
- **Development workflow optimization** - streamlined commands for common development tasks
- **Resource cleanup** - easy service shutdown and cleanup commands

### Production Deployment Automation
- **Webhook URL discovery** - automatically retrieves deployment webhooks from Coolify API
- **Environment variable management** - stores all service connection strings and webhook URLs
- **Deployment triggering** - single command deployment using stored webhook URLs
- **CI/CD integration** - GitHub Actions workflows use environment webhook variables

### Service Ecosystem
- **Complete infrastructure stack** - database, cache, AI services, and vector storage
- **Network isolation** - proper service networking with internal DNS resolution
- **Data persistence** - volumes configured for all stateful services
- **Security** - password protection and authentication for all services

## Benefits

- **Zero-configuration local development** - instant setup with comprehensive service stack
- **Automated deployment workflows** - webhook URLs automatically retrieved and stored
- **Enterprise-grade infrastructure** - proper networking, persistence, monitoring, and security
- **Developer productivity** - one-click setup, comprehensive documentation, and streamlined workflows
- **Production-ready architecture** - health checks, auto-deployment, and proper container configuration
- **Scalable service ecosystem** - complete AI, database, and cache infrastructure ready for use

The tool now provides complete end-to-end automation from local development setup to production deployment, with automatic webhook management and comprehensive infrastructure provisioning in Coolify.

body:
This PR adds support for specifying custom source directory paths via function parameters instead of deriving them automatically from the app name, addressing the feature request in issue #13.

## Changes Made

Added new function overloads to the main `ExIntegrationCoveralls` module:

### New Functions for `get_app_total_cov`:
- `get_app_total_cov/2` - accepts custom run-time source directory path
- `get_app_total_cov/3` - accepts both custom compile-time and run-time source directory paths

### New Functions for `post_app_cov_to_ci`:
- `post_app_cov_to_ci/4` - accepts custom run-time source directory path  
- `post_app_cov_to_ci/5` - accepts both custom compile-time and run-time source directory paths

## Usage Examples

```elixir
# Original functionality (unchanged for backward compatibility)
ExIntegrationCoveralls.get_app_total_cov("my_app")
ExIntegrationCoveralls.post_app_cov_to_ci(url, extends, "my_app")

# NEW: With custom run-time source directory path
ExIntegrationCoveralls.get_app_total_cov("my_app", "/custom/source/path")
ExIntegrationCoveralls.post_app_cov_to_ci(url, extends, "my_app", "/custom/source/path")

# NEW: With both custom compile-time and run-time source directory paths
ExIntegrationCoveralls.get_app_total_cov("my_app", "/compile/time/path", "/run/time/path")
ExIntegrationCoveralls.post_app_cov_to_ci(url, extends, "my_app", "/compile/time/path", "/run/time/path")
```

## Benefits

- **Flexible**: Users can now specify source paths via HTTP request parameters or function calls
- **Backward Compatible**: All existing functionality remains unchanged
- **Well-Tested**: Comprehensive test coverage following existing patterns
- **Documented**: Updated README with usage examples and benefits

This is particularly useful when:
- Source code is located in non-standard locations
- Analyzing coverage for specific subsets of the codebase
- Working with different paths for compile-time vs run-time environments

Fixes #13.

author: swyxio
body:
special PR for eric

Here’s a concise summary of the change set and the reason behind each edit.

What changed in `packages/build/src/extensions/prisma.ts`
1. Imported `readFileSync`  
   • Enables reading the contents of `schema.prisma` during `onBuildStart`.

2. Schema introspection & logging (inside `onBuildStart`)  
   • We now read the Prisma schema file and regex-extract every `generator` block’s `name`, `provider`, and (if present) `output`.  
   • The extracted data is written to the build logs (`context.logger.debug`).  
   • Wrapped in `try/catch`, emitting a warning instead of failing the build if parsing ever throws.

3. Extra log around “schema folder” detection (inside `onBuildComplete`)  
   • We already decide logic branches based on whether the schema’s parent folder is literally called `schema`.  
   • We now output the computed boolean plus the resolved path so it’s visible in the logs.

4. Minor TypeScript safety fix  
   • Cast `m[2]` to string and provided a default (`""`) to satisfy the linter when parsing regex matches.

Why we added these diagnostics
• Prisma v6.6+ introduces mandatory custom `output` paths and a new `prisma-client` generator.  
• Our extension’s current behaviour still assumes:  
  – Prisma client is generated in `node_modules`  (old default).  
  – A special `prisma/schema` folder pattern.  
• Before we refactor the logic we need hard evidence of what a project’s schema actually declares and which path is chosen at runtime.  
• The added logs will immediately show, during a build:  
  – Which generators exist (`prisma-client` or `prisma-client-js`).  
  – Whether a custom `output` path is configured.  
  – Whether our “schema-folder” heuristic triggered.  
• With that visibility we can confirm (or rule out) each of the failure hypotheses we listed and then implement the minimal behavioural changes with confidence.

No functional behaviour is changed yet—only richer debug output—so existing builds stay stable while we gather real-world data.

author: codewiththeflowxyz
body:
- Fixed stUSD balance not showing real-time accrued yield
- Switched from manual calculation to convertToAssets() contract method

  Problem

  The stUSD balance wasn't updating in real-time because the contract's chi
  (rate accumulator) only updates to storage during deposits/withdrawals.
  Users would see their balance suddenly "jump" after any transaction, rather
  than gradually increasing.

  Solution

  Use the contract's convertToAssets() function which calculates the current
  value including pending yield by computing what chi should be based on time
  elapsed, without requiring on-chain updates.

author: robodoig
body:
This PR addresses issue #73 and introduces the ability to randomise state choices either with or without replacement. A rule schema parameter is added that specifies whether the rule should perform state selection with or without replacement.

Two example rules (rule1.rule.yml and rule2.rule.yml) are provided that show how these changes can be used to implement:
1) block structure where each state must be chosen once before reset
2) completely random state selection

For the time being I've also simplified the state transition definition and removed the probability component. So far it seems that we are largely doing uniform sampling and the 1/n method for defining weighted probabilities previously was confusing and error prone. It's also not particularly compatible with the sampling without replacement method, but we can discuss how to add this back in if needed in the future.

author: rdesgroppes
body:
### What does this PR do? / Motivation
The present change is a follow-up of #39563, where it was found that:
> We need to have a default value here because these unit tests are also called from `macos` runners  but [`system` is patched as `linux`](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/39563/files#diff-407acb07e932b50660fc4999612d12a05d6046a1716a53125e1010050c898cebR33). So even though the unit tests are run in macos runners(run on EC2) they try to access vault and dont have K8 `POD_NAMESPACE` env var set.

It turns out the temporary fix introduced by #5010 in 2020 is no longer needed:
- upstream bug report: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/issues/1643
- upstream fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/1648
- released with `virtualenv` v20.0.5: https://virtualenv.pypa.io/en/latest/changelog.html#v20-0-5-2020-02-21

This therefore reverts commit d16a8a4da3baadc1ada4636513476e5b3df169cb: "[omnibus] Fix MacOS build conflicting with system Python 3 (#5010)", and adjusts consequences accordingly:
 - the `POD_NAMESPACE` environment variable must be present (no default) for `linux`, and only for `linux`,
- patches in tests get tailored to the very needs, with 3 `platforms` to cover implying 3 "sub" tests,
- covering `win32` unearthes unmatched command patterns due to suffixes (`.bat`, `.exe`) being used for certain commands (like `aws.exe` and `omnibus.bat`, unlike `git`) which requires further adaptation, especially to understand which patterns are not found.

This is the first PR to implement the semantics proposal: https://github.com/llvm/wg-hlsl/blob/main/proposals/0031-semantics.md

This PR focuses on the changes required to handle user semantics, but tried to be almost NFC.
What changes is the error messages as the semantics case is not kept when reporting error messages.

You might notice the SV_GroupIndex semantic is not properly validated as are others. This is an existing behavior that we'll need to fix, but wanted to keep this separated from this rewrite to stay as-close as an NFC as possible.

The next PR will add support on the different kinds of I/O we can have using semantics (input, inout param, structs).

body:
Replaces the dessant/lock-threads action with a direct GitHub Script implementation to avoid the deprecated search/issues API endpoint warning. The new implementation:
- Uses github.rest.issues.listForRepo() instead of the deprecated search API
- Maintains the same 7-day inactivity threshold
- Adds the same comment before locking
- Uses 'resolved' as the lock reason
- Handles pagination properly for large repositories

Replacing with custom implementation because we're [seeing](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/actions/runs/16806860705/job/47601485245) this deprecation warning:

It is scheduled to be removed on Thu, 04 Sep 2025 00:00:00 GMT. See https://github.blog/changelog/2025-03-06-github-issues-projects-api-support-for-issues-advanced-search-and-more/

author: runsonmypc
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces significant enhancements and critical bug fixes to the Motherlode Mine plugin, improving automation, flexibility, stability, and gem handling.

## Features Added
### 🎯 Deposit Box Support
- Added option to use deposit box instead of bank chest for faster ore depositing
- Smart deposit logic: uses `depositAll()` when no items need to be kept, `depositAllExcept()` otherwise
- Handles gem bag limitations with deposit box (empties to inventory first)

### 🔧 Automatic Pickaxe Detection
- Removed manual "Pick Axe In Inventory?" config option
- Plugin now automatically detects pickaxe location at startup (inventory vs equipped)
- Simplifies setup and reduces user configuration errors

### 👥 Configurable Player Avoidance
- Added optional anti-crashing mechanism for lower floor only
- Helps avoid unwanted attention from other players
- Defaults to OFF (since crashing is no longer an issue on lower floor)

### ⛏️ Ore Detection Before Mining
- Checks for actual ores in inventory before mining
- Automatically deposits any ores to maximize pay-dirt capacity
- Prevents inefficient mining with reduced inventory space

### 💎 Proper Gem Handling
- Gems collected during mining now stay in inventory (or go to gem bag)
- Only actual ores trigger banking during mining phase
- Both ores and gems are properly banked when emptying sack

### 🔨 Optional Waterwheel Repair
- Made waterwheel repair configurable (previously always on)
- Players can disable if they don't want to repair struts

### 🎨 UI Configuration Update
- Updated config panel to use blue box format with `@ConfigInformation`
- Consistent with other Microbot plugins

## Critical Bug Fixes
### 🐛 Fixed Shutdown Issues
- Changed `pickaxeName` initialization from empty string to `null` to prevent `depositAllExcept()` failures
- Added `isRunning()` check to `emptySack()` while loop for clean shutdown
- Fixed NullPointerException when checking pickaxe status

### 🏔️ Fixed Upper Floor Banking
- Added floor check before attempting to bank
- Prevents bot from trying to click bank/deposit box from upper floor

### 💎 Fixed Premature Gem Banking
- Split ore checking into two methods: ores-only and ores+gems
- Prevents unnecessary banking when gems are mined
- Gems now properly accumulate in inventory or gem bag

## Technical Improvements
- Removed redundant pickaxe withdrawal logic after banking
- Improved null handling throughout the codebase
- Better separation of concerns between equipped and inventory pickaxes
- Proper differentiation between ore and gem handling

## Testing Notes
- Tested with pickaxe equipped ✅
- Tested with pickaxe in inventory ✅
- Tested deposit box functionality ✅
- Tested player avoidance on lower floor ✅
- Tested ore detection and depositing ✅
- Tested gem collection without premature banking ✅
- Tested banking from upper floor prevention ✅
- Verified clean shutdown ✅

## Breaking Changes
- Removed `pickAxeInInventory` config option (now automatic)

The logic was moved into the ViewModel, ensuring dialog state is now driven by a single source of truth and tied to UI state updates. - Standardized success/error feedback: show toast on successful identifier creation and error UI on failures, all driven by a single sealed UI state and SharedFlow events. - Issue: Delete Identifier flow showed Loading twice; - Fix: Ensure a single collection per delete action and emit Loading once before the repository call; removed redundant state updates that caused duplicate emissions. Screenshots - Issue: Pull-to-refresh didn’t trigger loading on main screen; data refreshed silently. - Fix: Updated refreshIdentifiers in the ViewModel to explicitly set/loading/reset refresh state and emit a Loading UI state; UI now binds rememberPullRefreshState to the ViewModel’s refreshing flag. --- Testing notes - Create: Open Create Identifier, submit valid data → dialog dismisses, screen enters loading, success toast shows, list refreshes. - Delete: Delete an identifier → only one loading transition, no duplicate spinners. - Pull-to-refresh: Swipe down → screen enters loading, refresh indicator shows, content updates, indicator stops. --- ### Before: --- https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94365851-732a-4a00-b0ba-419c3511296e --- ### After: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0cebada9-2359-470e-8179-447709469b13 --- Please make sure these boxes are checked before submitting your pull request - thanks! - [ ] Run the static analysis check `./gradlew check` or `ci-prepush.sh` to make sure you didn't break anything - [ ] If you have multiple commits please combine them into one commit by squashing them. body:
# Summary 
- Allow more than one compressor to be applied to a given model
- Updates the `ModelCompressor.quantization_compressor` to now be a dictionary, such that more than one quantization compressor can be supported 
- Adds `mixed-precision` as a new `CompressionFormat` - if more than one format is found within the model, `mixed-precision` is set as the  model's  global format in its `config.json` 
- Adds `format` to the `QuantizationScheme` and leverages this per-module format field in order to fetch the appropriate compressor to compress the model
- Note: this is not supported for `ModelCompressor.compress` and `ModelCompressor.decompress` - only `compress_model` and `decompress_model` currently support this functionality as compress/decompress essentially only support global formats

# Testing:
- nightly passes

# Next Steps:
- Decompression for mixed-precision is currently not supported - we will eventually need this to run lm-evals/hf forward passes

# Example Updates
- For an NVFP4 + FP8 model, the recipe could look like this
```yaml
quant_stage:
    quant_modifiers:
        QuantizationModifier:
            ignore: ["lm_head"]
            config_groups:
                group_0:
                    weights:
                        num_bits: 8
                        type: float
                        strategy: channel
                        dynamic: false
                        symmetric: true
                    input_activations:
                        num_bits: 8
                        type: float
                        strategy: token
                        dynamic: true
                        symmetric: true
                    targets: ["re:.*mlp.down_proj.*"]
                group_1:
                    weights:
                        num_bits: 4
                        type: float
                        strategy: tensor_group
                        dynamic: false
                        symmetric: true
                        group_size: 16
                    input_activations:
                        num_bits: 4
                        type: float
                        strategy: tensor_group
                        dynamic: local
                        symmetric: true
                        group_size: 16

"""
